Admit.
With the consent of parties heard finally on appeal.

The appellant/claimant has filed this Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 for enhancement of the compensation amount being aggrieved with the award dated 28/02/2023 passed by Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jabalpur in MACC No.1082/2018, by which the learned Claims Tribunal awarded a total sum of Rs.1,73,160/- (one lakhs seventy three thousand one hundred sixty) only with 6% interest to the appellant/claimant by way of compensation for the injuries, which she has sustained in a motor vehicle accident.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. According to claimant i.e. appellant herein, the compensation awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal is on lower side and hence, need to be enhanced.

3. Since, this appeal is for the enhancement in the compensation amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal, hence the question that arises for consideration is whether any case for enhancement in compensation awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal on facts and evidence adduced, is made out and if so to what extent ?
4.
It is not necessary to narrate the entire facts in detail, such as how the accident occurred, who was negligent in driving the offending vehicle, who is liable for paying compensation etc.
It is for the reason that firstly all these findings are recorded in favour of appellant/claimant by the Tribunal.

Secondly, the findings though recorded in favour of claimant are not under challenge at the instance of any of the respondents such as owner/driver or insurance company either by way of filing an appeal or cross-objection.
In this view of the matter, there is no justification to burden this order by detailing facts on all these issues.

5. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that in a motor accident which took place on 12/11/2017 the appellant sustained multiple injuries including fracture in her left hand and teeth were also broken and learned Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.Rs.1,73,157/- (one lakhs seventy three thousand one hundred fifty seven), which was rounded off Rs.1,73,160/- (One lakhs seventy three thousand one hundred sixty), breakup of which is as under :
Rs.5,000/- Towards loss of income during treatment Rs.1,05,840/- Towards loss of income due to permanent disability Rs.22,317/- Towards medical expenses Rs.15,000/- Towards special diet, attendant & transportation expenses Rs.25,000/-
Pain and sufferings and loss of amenities in life and the happiness,
6. Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that due to motorcycle accident appellant has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 20%, in this regard disability certificate (Ex. P/10) has been filed, which is proved by statement of Dr. Sharad Dwivedi (AW 2), who has stated that the appellant suffered 20% permanent disability.
However, the Tribunal has wrongly assessed the permanent disability as 7% in paragraph 24 of impugned award.
Learned counsel for the appellant also submitted that under the head of grievous injury no amount has been awarded and meager amount has been awarded in other heads, which should be enhanced.

2 7.

Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No. 2 opposed the prayer and submits that the learned Tribunal has awarded sufficient amount to the appellant after appreciating the evidence placed on record.
Hence, he prays for dismissal of appeal.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

9. From perusal of record it appears that the appellant/claimant remained hospitalized for three days, hence the amount awarded under the head of loss of income during treatment, attendant,
special diet, transportation expenses and in the head of pain and suffering are just and proper.

Dr.
Sharad Dwivedi (AW-2) has admitted that he has given the certificate for permanent disability of 20% only for left hand and he could not say about the disability for the whole body, hence it is not proved that appellant suffered 20% permanent disability in relation to the whole body.
Hence, this Court finds that the learned tribunal has rightly awarded amount under the head of loss of future income.

10. However, from perusal of record it appears that the learned tribunal has not awarded any amount in the head of grievous injury caused to the appellant in the alleged incident, which should be awarded.
Hence, in the head of grievous injury as caused to the appellant in the alleged incident in her left hand a sum of Rs.40,000/- (Forty thousand) is awarded.

11. Taking this view of the matter, present appeal stands disposed of with a direction that in addition to the amount already awarded by learned Claims Tribunal, respondent No.3-Insurance Company shall pay an additional sum of Rs.40,000/- (Forty thousand) in favour of the appellant alongwith interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of actual payment.
12. Respondent No.3/Insurance Company is directed to pay the enhanced amount within a period of sixty days from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
13. Other terms and conditions of the award shall remain intact.
14. Records of the claims Tribunal be sent back alongwith the copy of this order for information and necessary compliance.
No order as to costs.

(AMAR NATH (KESHARWANI)) JUDGE as.
